title: Clinical Burden of Disease of Norovirus Infections in German Hospitals: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
summary:
Norovirus is one of the most common causes of acute gastroenteritis (vomiting and diarrhea) and can lead to severe illness, particularly in older adults, people with weakened immune systems, and hospitalized patients. However, little is known about the overall burden of norovirus infections in German hospitals.

The aim of this study is to better understand how norovirus infections affect patients treated in German hospitals. The study will evaluate patient characteristics, underlying medical conditions, laboratory findings, treatments, the course of the illness, length of hospital stay, and possible complications. In addition, the study will assess how long norovirus can remain detectable after the initial infection.

The study will use existing information from the electronic medical records of patients who were diagnosed with norovirus infection during routine clinical care. No additional examinations, tests, or study-related procedures will be performed, and participation will not involve any additional burden or risk for patients.

interventions.name: This study is an exploratory retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted at five tertiary care university hospitals in Germany.
